title: Ohio Maritime Assistance Program (MAP)
eligible_entities: Public port authorities owning an active marine cargo terminal on Lake Erie or the Ohio River (per ORC 5501.91)
summary: Competitive ODOT grant exclusively for Ohio public port authorities to enhance waterborne freight, expand cargo-handling capacity, and rehabilitate maritime infrastructure. The Port of Cleveland was awarded $4.2M in Jan 2026 ($2.7M for Dock 22 rehab; $1.5M for the CHEERS Early Action Breakwater Project).
notes: Requires 50% local match. FY22-23 funded at $23M; reduced ~60% for FY24-25 biennium. Program-to-date (FY20-25) ~$56M leveraging $145M across 21 projects among 4 public port authorities. Single best-fit program for the Port.

title: Ohio Brownfield Remediation Program (BRP)
match_required: Generally none for county set-aside funds
eligible_entities: Per ORC §122.6511(A)(2): county; township; municipal corporation; port authority; conservancy district; park district; county land reutilization corporation; for-profit organizations
summary: Grants to assess and clean up industrial/commercial brownfield sites for redevelopment. HB96/ODOD FY26 guidelines: $200M total ($100M per fiscal year). FY26 has $88M available with $1M reserved for applicants in each of Ohio's 88 counties; FY27 ~$109M available statewide on merit.
notes: May 18–June 5, 2026 round draws on set-asides remaining in 46 counties. Port authorities are explicitly eligible lead entities; recent example: Guernsey County Port Authority awarded $1M. Cuyahoga County historically wins 25-50% of statewide funds.

title: Ohio Building Demolition & Site Revitalization Program
match_required: Yes — 25% for non-set-aside (statewide) funds; none for county set-aside
eligible_entities: Counties via designated lead entity (county land bank by default); subrecipients including port authorities
summary: Funds demolition of vacant/blighted commercial and residential structures (non-brownfield sites) and revitalization of surrounding properties. ~$230,000 reserved per county; $20-21.5M per fiscal year (HB96 appropriated $20M/year).
notes: Cuyahoga County land bank is the default lead entity; the Port would participate as a subrecipient. 25% match applies only to statewide first-come-first-served funds.

title: ODOT Transportation Review Advisory Council (TRAC) — Major New Capacity Program
match_required: No fixed %, but local funding commitment is scored
eligible_entities: Public agencies: municipalities; county commissioners; county engineers; transit and port authorities; transportation improvement districts
summary: Funds Ohio's Major New Capacity Program for projects over $12M that add capacity or reduce congestion; eligible project types explicitly include intermodal port and rail projects. Recent cycles: FY2026 ~$123.1M (11 projects); 2025 ~$319.3M (14 projects).
notes: Port authorities EXPLICITLY eligible; freight scoring uses port metrics (TEUs, bulk tons). Annual May 1–31 application window. Strong fit for large intermodal capital projects.

title: ODNR Coastal Management Assistance Grant (CMAG)
agency: Ohio Department of Natural Resources, Office of Coastal Management
eligible_entities: Units of local government; counties; regional planning agencies; park districts; conservancy districts; educational institutions; nonprofits
summary: Competitive annual reimbursement grant for Lake Erie coastal projects: water quality, coastal planning, public access, habitat restoration, and redevelopment of deteriorating waterfronts and ports. ~$200K-$500K total available per cycle; typical requests $25K-$150K.
notes: NOAA-funded but state-administered; program text explicitly references redevelopment of deteriorating waterfronts and ports. Preference for beneficial use of dredged material — directly aligned with CHEERS.

title: Clean Ohio Green Space Conservation Program
agency: Ohio Public Works Commission (District 1 / Cuyahoga NRAC)
match_required: Up to 75% funded (25% match; land/labor/materials count as match)
eligible_entities: Local governments; park districts; watershed nonprofits; political subdivisions
summary: Grants for green space acquisition and protection/enhancement of river and stream corridors. Cuyahoga County (District 1) has ~$3.2M allocated for FY2027 (Round 21).
notes: Apply through Cuyahoga County NRAC. Match can be funding, land, labor, or materials. Annual cycle (next ~fall 2026).

title: OPWC State Capital Improvement Program (SCIP / Issue 1-Issue 2)
match_required: Varies; leverages local funds ($1 program : $2-3 local typical)
eligible_entities: Counties; cities; villages; townships; political subdivisions
summary: Bond-funded grants and loans for local infrastructure — roads, bridges, water/wastewater, storm water. Voter-renewed program; up to $250M per year statewide distributed to local districts by population.
notes: Apply via District 1 (Cuyahoga). Port roads, utilities, and storm water eligible as public infrastructure. District 1 deadline historically early October.

title: Local Transportation Improvement Program (LTIP)
eligible_entities: Counties; cities; villages; townships; political subdivisions
summary: Gas-tax-funded program (~$70M/year statewide) for local road and bridge improvements; companion to SCIP, distributed by OPWC district.
notes: Funds roads/bridges only. Apply via District 1.

title: NOACA Transportation for Livable Communities Initiative (TLCI) — Planning
eligible_entities: Political subdivisions; state agencies; boards; commissions; regional transit authorities; county transit boards; port authorities
summary: Funds planning studies for integrated transportation/land-use and community livability. Port authorities explicitly listed as eligible.
notes: Applications normally open in October. TLCI Planning Assistance (NOACA staff time in lieu of a grant) is also available. Strong fit for lakefront/connectivity studies.

title: NOACA TLCI — Implementation
match_required: Yes — 20% from non-federal sources (awards funded at max 80%)
eligible_entities: Political subdivisions; port authorities; RTAs; municipalities
summary: Implementation awards to build infrastructure from completed TLCI livability studies; minimum requests $100,000.
notes: Requires a prior TLCI plan. 20% local match.

title: NOACA Surface Transportation Block Grant (STBG) / Transportation Alternatives set-aside
eligible_entities: Political subdivisions; port authorities; transit agencies; ODOT; county engineers
summary: NOACA allocates ~$51M/year in federal-aid funds to regional highway, transit, freight, and transportation-alternatives projects; port authorities eligible to sponsor.
notes: Federally sourced but regionally programmed by the MPO (overlooked regional discretion). Plan amended annually; TIP updated every two years.

title: NEORSD Green Infrastructure Grant Program
eligible_entities: Member communities; governmental entities; 501(c)(3) nonprofits; businesses partnering with communities in the combined sewer area
summary: Grants up to $250,000 for green-infrastructure stormwater projects (bioretention, permeable pavement, green roofs, cisterns) that remove stormwater from the combined sewer system. Since 2014, NEORSD has allocated $10.7M capturing 32.5M gallons of annual runoff.
notes: Project must be in the combined-sewer service area (includes much of Cleveland). Reimbursement basis; pre-proposal meeting earns scoring points.

title: Lake Erie Protection Fund (LEPF)
eligible_entities: Research institutions; nonprofits; local governments; counties; municipalities; agencies
summary: Grants for research and on-the-ground projects that protect, preserve, and restore Lake Erie and its watershed; funded in part by Lake Erie license plate sales. Grants up to ~$50,000.
notes: Annual cycle. Smaller grants suited to shoreline/habitat pilots and feasibility work.

title: Lake Erie Community Grant (LECG)
eligible_entities: Local governments; counties; municipalities; nonprofits; tribes; research/academic institutions
summary: Funds community-driven habitat restoration, stream daylighting, invasive species control, and stormwater projects in Ohio's Lake Erie watershed. ~12 small grants up to $75K and two large up to $750K. CMNH received $750K for Mentor Marsh restoration in Apr 2026.
notes: GLRI-funded (federal pass-through) but administered by the state commission. Next round opened Feb 10, 2026; due April 30, 2026.

title: H2Ohio (Statewide Wetland / Water Quality Initiative)
agency: ODNR / Ohio EPA / Ohio Dept. of Agriculture (with Ohio Lake Erie Commission)
match_required: Up to 100% reimbursement for wetland projects
eligible_entities: Local governments; port authorities; nonprofits; SWCDs; agricultural partners
summary: Governor DeWine's statewide water-quality initiative funding wetland restoration, natural infrastructure, drinking-water/wastewater, and nutrient reduction. H2Ohio provided $500K to the Mentor Marsh Coastal Restoration Project (CMNH).
notes: Multiple sub-programs across agencies. Port can pursue wetland/shoreline restoration; Toledo-Lucas County Port Authority partnered on H2Ohio wetland work (Duck Creek).

title: Ohio Environmental Education Fund (OEEF)
agency: Ohio EPA, Office of Environmental Education
eligible_entities: State and local governments; schools; colleges; nonprofits; businesses; trade organizations
summary: Grants for environmental education projects targeting students, the public, and the regulated community. Mini grants $500-$5,000; general grants up to $50,000; ~$500,000-$700,000 annually.
notes: Funded by air/water pollution civil penalties. Good fit for Port maritime/community environmental education programming.

title: ODNR Coastal — Erosion / Estuarine Land Conservation (CELCP)
agency: Ohio Department of Natural Resources, Office of Coastal Management
eligible_entities: Local subdivisions; agencies
summary: One-time Erosion Emergency Assistance Grants ($5M in state capital funds) for shoreline erosion control to preserve health/safety; CELCP funded coastal land acquisition (federal funding currently dormant).
notes: CELCP federal funding has lapsed for years and erosion grants were a one-time appropriation. Low confidence on current availability — monitor for future capital-budget revivals.

title: Ohio Rail Development Commission (ORDC) Rail Grants
eligible_entities: Companies; railroads; port authorities; local governments
summary: Grants to preserve/expand freight rail service, rehabilitate track and bridges, build spurs, and improve crossings. Port authorities have received ORDC support (e.g., Sandusky County-Seneca County-City of Tiffin Port Authority's 24-mile rail line).
notes: Rolling board approvals (recent awards $150K-$1.2M). Directly relevant to Port intermodal/rail connectivity (Cleveland Bulk Terminal, dock rail).

title: Ohio EPA Diesel Mitigation Trust Fund / Diesel Emissions Reduction Grant (DMTF/DERG)
match_required: Yes — minimum 25% (DMTF) / 20% (DERG) from non-state, non-federal sources
eligible_entities: Public and private fleet owners; port cargo-handling equipment operators; locomotive/ferry owners
summary: Grants to replace or repower older diesel engines, including port cargo-handling equipment, freight-switcher locomotives, ferries, and Class 4-8 trucks. $50,000-$2,000,000 per project.
notes: Port cargo-handling equipment and switcher locomotives are EXPLICITLY eligible — a strong decarbonization fit. DMTF is VW-settlement funded; DERG is CMAQ-funded.

title: TechCred (Ohio)
agency: Ohio Department of Development / Governor's Office of Workforce Transformation
eligible_entities: Any Ohio employer with W-2 employees (state agencies excluded; political-subdivision eligibility to be confirmed)
summary: Reimburses employers up to $2,000 per credential for employee technology-focused training; up to $30,000 per round and $180,000 per year. Bimonthly application rounds.
notes: Caution: Agencies of the State of Ohio are not eligible. The Port (a political subdivision/local authority) should confirm eligibility before relying on this. Useful to upskill maritime/logistics staff.

title: JobsOhio Workforce Grant
eligible_entities: Companies in JobsOhio target industries; partners
summary: Reimburses training costs to improve worker skills tied to job creation/retention; decisions based on job creation, payroll, and investment.
notes: Geared to private companies; the Port could partner with tenants/employers rather than apply directly.

title: JobsOhio Economic Development Grant
eligible_entities: Companies in target industries with job creation/fixed-asset investment
summary: Funds fixed-asset and infrastructure investment for business expansion and job creation; reimbursement-based.
notes: Company-focused; Port relevant as a development partner/landowner. Excludes retail/population-driven businesses.

title: JobsOhio Revitalization Program (Loan & Grant Fund)
eligible_entities: Businesses; nonprofits; local governments controlling a site with a redevelopment/job plan
summary: Loans and grants (including Phase II assessments) to redevelop brownfield/underutilized sites where redevelopment cost exceeds land value; projects typically retain/create 20+ jobs.
notes: Local governments eligible where they commit the project. Useful for Port-owned redevelopment parcels.

title: Ohio Air Quality Development Authority (OAQDA) — Clean Air Improvement Program (CAIP)
match_required: Varies; grant subsidies offset bond financing
eligible_entities: Cities; counties; municipalities; businesses; governmental agencies
summary: Tax-exempt conduit bond financing plus grant subsidies for air-quality, energy-efficiency, and renewable-energy facilities; OAQDA may make loans and grants to governmental agencies for the acquisition/construction of air quality facilities.
notes: Primarily conduit bond financing with grant offsets; small-business CARC offers grants up to ~$20K. The Port could finance clean-energy/efficiency upgrades. Largely a financing vehicle, not a pure grant.

title: Ohio Water Development Authority (OWDA) — Fresh Water / Local Economic Development Loan
eligible_entities: Local governments; industries via the Local Economic Development (LED) Loan
summary: Below-market loans (not grants) for water, wastewater, and storm-water infrastructure; the LED Loan funds water/sewer projects tied to significant investment and job creation. Applications accepted monthly with same-month approval possible.
notes: Loans not grants; included as an overlooked non-federal capital source. Prevailing wage applies to LED projects.

title: OWDA Research & Development Grant Program
eligible_entities: Governmental agencies; research entities
summary: Grants under OWDA's authority to engage in research and development related to environmental/water infrastructure.
notes: Limited public detail on size and cycle; low confidence — verify directly with OWDA before relying on it.

title: Ohio Capital Budget — Community Project Funding
agency: Ohio General Assembly / Ohio Office of Budget and Management
eligible_entities: Government entities and nonprofits with capital projects and a state nexus
summary: Biennial legislative earmarks (~$150-200M total per biennium) for local capital improvements (construction, acquisition, infrastructure), secured by petitioning state legislators.
notes: Not a competitive agency grant — access is via legislative advocacy; current cycle deadline to legislators was March 12, 2026. The Port qualifies as a government entity for capital projects. Funded by state bond proceeds (tax-law compliance for life of bonds).

title: NOACA Brownfields Revolving Loan Fund (RLF)
eligible_entities: Applicants in the 12-county NE Ohio region (incl. Cuyahoga) owning/controlling eligible sites
summary: Loans and sub-grants to clean up hazardous substances or petroleum at brownfield sites; federally capitalized by US EPA but administered regionally by NOACA.
notes: An overlooked local source distinct from grants.gov listings. Quarterly review by the Brownfields Steering Committee.

title: The Cleveland Foundation — Environment / Economic Transformation Grants
eligible_entities: 501(c)(3) nonprofits and government agencies in Cuyahoga, Lake, and Geauga counties
summary: Community foundation grants in priority areas including Environment (freshwater/water quality, clean energy) and Economic Transformation; supports government agencies and nonprofits. Four annual deadlines (Mar 31, Jun 30, Sep 15, Dec 31).
notes: Government agencies are eligible. The Responsive Grants program was temporarily paused — verify current status. Port could apply or partner for lakefront/environment work.

title: The George Gund Foundation — Climate Justice / Economic Justice Grants
eligible_entities: Primarily 501(c)(3) nonprofits in Greater Cleveland; capital grants are nonprofit-only and require LEED certification
summary: Private foundation grants in Climate Justice and Economic Justice (community revitalization, parks/public space, waterfront redevelopment), made over three board cycles per year; funded Irishtown Bend Park along the Cuyahoga River via a nonprofit partner.
notes: The Port (a political subdivision, not a 501(c)(3)) would likely need a nonprofit partner; capital grants require both nonprofit status and LEED certification. Verify eligibility with a program officer. Grant-range figures are from third-party funder databases.
